Issued at 128 AM EDT Mon Oct 12 2026

             -----------Synoptic Overview-----------

A surface cold front sits roughly from Melbourne to Venice. Little
to no cold air advection is occurring behind the boundary; it is
the leading edge of drier continental air slowly moving southward
down the peninsula. The front is tied to a mid-level shortwave
trough axis extending from the Mid-Atlantic states to the NE Gulf.

Elongated ridging, with H5 heights around 594 dam, is situated 
from the Bahamas to the Gulf. Over the next 36 hours, the western 
extent of this ridge will expand northward toward Texas and 
Louisiana, resulting in light northwesterly mid-level flow over 
Florida. This setup will allow the front to clear the district 
later today and usher in below-normal PWAT (total moisture) values
over Florida through at least Wednesday.

Cluster analysis of the 11/12Z grand ensemble indicates excellent
model agreement through at least Friday. Broad ridging should remain
in place over the Southeast U.S. as a weak inverted trough passes
from the Caribbean Sea into the Bay of Campeche. Amid moderate
onshore flow, a gradual increase in moisture is expected between 
late Wednesday and Friday, especially over the southern half of 
the state.

Guidance appears to be coming into better agreement with the
pattern evolution this weekend. A shortwave is expected to pass
from the Canadian Prairies into the Great Lakes by Friday. This
disturbance has trended more progressive, limiting phasing with
a cut-off low over the Rockies. As the disturbance reaches New
England by Saturday, its cold front is forecast to reach Central
Florida. Slightly above-normal moisture may lift over the area ahead
of the front. Following the front, a 1030 hPa surface high will 
move across the Ohio Valley. With this trajectory, fresh onshore 
breezes are forecast to develop behind the front. This will likely
prevent significant dry or cold air advection with the frontal 
passage.

             -------Sensible Weather & Impacts-------

Today - Tuesday...

The slow-moving front will slip south of the area today, with
abundant sunshine except for the Treasure Coast where clearing
will be slower through the day. There is a low chance of showers
over St Lucie and Martin Counties this morning before the moisture
thins out. Dew points should dip into the 60s across most of the
area, making our highs in the mid to upper 80s feel much more
comfortable. Most spots will fall into the mid-upper 60s tonight,
except perhaps right along the coast (near 70).

Onshore flow tries to become established on Tuesday. As this occurs,
some moisture is forecast to return to the boundary layer. The
main consequence should be intervals of cloud cover, though a few
sprinkles or brief showers also cannot be ruled out. Staying warm
with highs in the mid-upper 80s.

Wednesday - Friday...

Additional moisture slowly lifts from south to north during
the second half of the week as onshore flow continues over
the peninsula. This appears sufficient for a daily chance of
showers, especially over the southern half of the area on Thursday
(30-50%). By Friday, instability increases a bit more, so we may
begin to see a few storms develop in the afternoon, especially
closer to Lake Okeechobee. Rain chances range from 20% north of
Orlando to 60% near Lake Okeechobee to end the work week.

Highs in the mid to upper 80s should continue. By Friday, heat
indices ramp up again, closing in on 100 degrees south of Orlando.

Weekend...

As the next cold front settles into Florida, it should be
weakening. What remains uncertain is how far northward moisture
will return ahead of the boundary. This will determine the coverage
of showers and storms on Saturday. Drier postfrontal air may have
difficulty advancing much south of I-4 as onshore flow redevelops
by Sunday.

Speaking of the onshore flow, this could set up a rather windy
period from Sunday into next Monday as strong high pressure sets up
a tight gradient over the state. If this regime plays out, one could
expect rounds of gusty showers moving off the Atlantic. Hazardous
beach and boating conditions are also likely to develop.

Statistical guidance suggests high temperatures will trend slightly
cooler, especially by next Sunday, with some mid-upper 70s along
and north of I-4.
